name: Duolingo Super
tagline: Build a small user-authored language practice deck with spaced repetition and pronunciation recordin

pricing.notes: Typical US monthly Super price; regional and family pricing differs.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Duolingo Super, build a small user-authored language practice deck with spaced repetition and pronunciation recording. The hard boundary is massive curriculum, adaptive models, content, social loops, mobile polish, and brand, plus content, pedagogy, and network.
coreLoopDIY: Build a small user-authored language practice deck, schedule spaced retrieval practice with pronunciation recording, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
requirements: optional speech or language-model API key
whatYouLose: massive curriculum, adaptive models, content, social loops, mobile polish, and brand
ongoingBurden: curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Duolingo Super because the learning loop is buildable, while trusted curriculum, instructors, feedback, credentials, and community are not. The recurring cost buys curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Moodle
priorArt.desc: Long-running open-source learning platform with courses, assessments, and progress tracking.

alternatives.name: Anki
alternatives.desc: Build a small language deck with audio, images, typed answers and excellent spaced repetition; no cartoon guilt trips.

facts.install: Use the Windows installer, macOS DMG or official Linux launcher
facts.dataFormat: Local profile files including collection.anki2, collection.media and backups; exports use .apkg/.colpkg, with optional AnkiWeb sync
facts.gapVsPaid: Anki has no supplied course, game loop, social competition or polished pronunciation exercises; the user authors or imports the deck.

alternatives.name: AnkiDroid
alternatives.desc: A full Android Anki client for authored language decks, pronunciation recordings and offline review.

facts.install: Install from Google Play or F-Droid, or sideload the official APK
facts.dataFormat: An Anki collection and media on the Android device, with .apkg import/export and optional AnkiWeb sync
facts.gapVsPaid: AnkiDroid has no supplied gamified course or social progression, and it is an Android client rather than a cross-platform lesson service.

alternatives.name: FreeLingo
alternatives.desc: A Duolingo-shaped course runner with CEFR lessons, voice exercises and spaced review; self-hosting is the price of unlimited use.

facts.install: Use the hosted service, or run Docker Compose with PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7 and the configured AI/speech services
facts.engines: Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic or DeepSeek for language generation; Kokoro or OpenAI TTS; faster-whisper or OpenAI Whisper for speech recognition
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted data in PostgreSQL, transient state in Redis, and generated/cached MP3 files; managed accounts live in FreeLingo's cloud
facts.gapVsPaid: FreeLingo's course quality, gamification, social features and editorial maturity are far behind Duolingo, while serious self-hosted voice practice requires substantial infrastructure.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker plus an Ollama model or API keys; production voice also needs HTTPS, WebSocket proxying and either GPU-backed local models or paid APIs

alternatives.name: Moodle
alternatives.desc: Can run your own sequenced lessons, quizzes and progress tracking, though nobody will mistake it for a game.

facts.install: Upload the PHP release to a web server, create a database and moodledata directory, then complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Courses, users, grades and settings in SQL; uploaded files in the separate moodledata directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Moodle has no game-quality language curriculum, streak loop or adaptive exercise polish and is vastly heavier to administer.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP and database requirements, protected writable storage, cron, SMTP, backups and upgrades are all the operator's responsibility

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Super plan and a personal study companion DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Duolingo Super in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and a service worker for offline use; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: build a small user-authored language practice deck, schedule spaced retrieval practice with pronunciation recording, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Import Markdown, text, or user-authored notes and split them into editable learning units.
Create flashcards and short quizzes only after showing the generated items for approval.
Implement a transparent spaced-repetition schedule with due, again, hard, good, and easy actions.
Add goals, study sessions, streak-free progress charts, notes, and weak-topic review.
For language practice, record the learner and compare timing or pronunciation without presenting medical claims.
Support offline use, full export, reset, backup, and deletion of all learning data.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out licensed premium courses.
Deliberately leave out accredited certificates and grading.
Deliberately leave out live tutors, large classrooms, and a learner marketplace.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
